headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection/data-flow exposure only if these docs are manually bridged; otherwise the pair is largely non-interactive and low risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both profiles are documentation-only and show no shared channel by default: agent_a has allowlisted network egress, while agent_b has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, files, or MCP. A prompt-injection pathway would require unusual manual copy-paste or an external bridge, so the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies agent_a output into agent_b prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added outside these profiles, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Avoid copy-pasting untrusted agent_a output into agent_b.
Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any ad hoc shared clipboard or relay.
Review agent_a outputs before reuse.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: No plausible data-leak path is documented: agent_a touches no data classes and only has allowlisted egress, while agent_b has no file, clipboard, stdin/stdout, or API surfaces and no secrets handled. Without a shared workspace or transport, there is no route for sensitive data to flow between them.
conditions: IF either profile is connected to a shared workspace or external transport not listed here, reassess leakage.
IF agent_a begins handling sensitive data classes, the conclusion no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep both agents disconnected from shared storage.
Do not route sensitive documents through either agent.
Confirm agent_b remains local documentation-only.
Audit any future API or file connectors before enabling.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls if a shared channel is introduced.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: There is no overlapping write surface to conflict over. Agent_a exposes only allowlisted network egress and agent_b explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, or use MCP. With no shared mutable resource, concurrent capability conflict is provably absent.
conditions: IF agent_a is later given filesystem, git, or database write access, conflict analysis must be redone.
IF a shared mutable resource is added outside these profiles, conflict becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep agent_b read-only as configured.
Do not grant agent_a write access to shared state.
Avoid running both against the same mutable repo.
Document any future shared resource ownership.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent_b is a content-writing/reference profile with no action-taking tools, so it is unlikely to blindly execute agent_a outputs. Agent_a can emit content over allowlisted egress, but without a downstream actuator in agent_b the cascade is limited to mistaken prose rather than operational harm.
conditions: IF agent_b is later used to auto-commit, email, or call APIs based on agent_a text, the severity increases.
IF agent_a output is treated as authoritative without review, error propagation becomes more likely.
mitigations: Require human review of agent_a outputs before reuse.
Keep agent_b in drafting mode only.
Do not connect agent_b to action-taking tools.
Add a checklist for factual verification.
requires-engineering: add citation validation before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced: both profiles are open-source, docs-only, and touch no data classes. Agent_a has allowlisted egress and agent_b has no network egress or secrets handling, so there is no documented residency, retention, or regulated-data pathway to compare.
conditions: IF either agent begins processing regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, compliance must be reassessed.
IF a future deployment adds retention or residency constraints, compare them explicitly.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Record any future data-class changes.
Verify deployment region before enabling sensitive workflows.
Retain only minimal logs.
requires-engineering: add policy checks for regulated data flows.
